title: feat: let child keys create keys
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Keys created with an API key (`POST /account/keys`) now keep the `keys` account permission when `accountPermissions` requests it; before, it was silently stripped
- Removes the now-unused `allowAccountKeysPermission` flag
- Updates the route, CLI, SDK and skill docs that said `keys` is auto-stripped
- Why: a hosted machine's key (#15251) needs to mint a dedicated `polli harness` key inside the VM; harness keys themselves never request `keys`

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Child created with `accountPermissions: ["keys"]` | `keys` stripped | `keys` kept |
| Child created without `keys` | no `keys` | no `keys` |
| Key without `account:keys` calling `POST /account/keys` | 403 | 403 |

A key holding `keys` could already create unbudgeted keys, so no key gains more power than its root. `APIDOCS.md` regenerates after the production deploy.

Tests: `test/integration/account-keys.test.ts` 15/15; gen typecheck clean.

gist.headline: Keys can plant keys
gist.blurb: Child API keys can now carry the `keys` permission when their parent deliberately grants it. A hosted machine can mint its own dedicated Polli harness key without the permission vanishing into the mulch.
gist.summary: `POST /account/keys` now preserves `accountPermissions: ["keys"]` for children created by an API key, enabling delegated key creation while keys that do not request `keys` remain unchanged and callers without `account:keys` still receive 403.
gist.impact: Hosted machines with an explicitly delegated `keys` permission can create scoped harness keys inside their environment, with no new authority granted beyond what the root key already allowed.
gist.visual_concept: Depict delegated API-key creation as a cozy greenhouse: Polli tends a parent key plant that grows a smaller, clearly labeled harness-key seedling only when it carries the `keys` badge. A friendly CRT monitor robot can carefully stamp the permission onto the seed packet, while a locked gate in the background represents the unchanged 403 boundary for keys without permission.
